# opencode-island A **Dynamic Island** for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai), on macOS and Windows. Windows support is new: the island builds and runs there, and the limits below are the ones we know about. If something does not work on your machine, please open an issue. It floats on the right edge of your screen and tells you what every session and agent on your machine is doing — and lets you answer a permission prompt without ever leaving the window you are working in. **→ [opencode-island.github.io](https://hamzasoussi53.github.io/opencode-island/)** ![The island expanded, showing a running session](docs/panel.png) - **Closed**, it is a thin vertical tab on the right edge with the status reading down its spine. - **Open** it (click it) and it becomes a drawer listing the sessions running right now, with their subagents nested underneath. - **Talk to it** — the drawer has a composer at its foot. Type a prompt and press Enter, and the agent picks it up where it is. - **Approvals** turn the whole island warning orange, open it by themselves, and can be answered in place. - **Alive** — every session that is busy carries a small orb that says what it is doing: thinking, writing, searching, running code. - **Live** — the last ten words the agent is saying scroll down the closed tab as they arrive. --- ## Requirements | | | |---|---| | macOS | 13 or newer | | Windows | 10 or newer, x64 (ARM64 is untested) | | OpenCode | 2.2.7 or newer (the GUI plugin API) | | Node | 22.18 or newer to build from source, 24 or newer to run `npm run check` | The island is a plugin: it uses an Electron window that floats above other apps. On macOS it floats above full-screen apps and every Space too. ## Install ### With the OpenCode CLI (recommended) ```sh opencode plugin add opencode-island ``` That installs the package and adds it to your global OpenCode config. Restart the desktop app and the island appears on the right edge of your primary display. To remove it again: ```sh opencode plugin remove opencode-island ``` The CLI also takes a Git specifier, which builds the plugin from source: ```sh opencode plugin add github:hamzasoussi53/opencode-island ``` ### From source ```sh git clone https://github.com/hamzasoussi53/opencode-island cd opencode-island npm install --ignore-scripts npm run build ln -s "$PWD" ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-island ``` On Windows the symlink needs Developer Mode or an elevated shell, and in Git Bash `ln -s` copies the folder instead, so the plugin stops updating. `opencode plugin add github:hamzasoussi53/opencode-island` avoids all of it. `--ignore-scripts` skips Electron's ~100 MB binary download. The plugin only needs Electron's type declarations to build; the desktop app supplies the runtime. A plain `npm install` works too, it just downloads the binary as well. ## Use ### The closed tab The tab sits on the right edge, vertically centred. It shows one line: - `2 agents working` — how many agents are busy right now - `1 approval needed` — somebody is waiting for you - `Idle` — nothing is running Next to the grip, a small orb shows what the busiest session is doing, and the words fill the tab without ever changing its length: the newest ones stay in sight and the oldest are cut off at the top. Under the grip, a number counts the agents that are working, and pops when the count changes. Under that, the steps of the agent's plan: the one before, the one in hand and the one after, each a number and a dot. Green when the step is done, orange and pulsing on the step in hand, yellow for the ones waiting, red for the one that failed. Open the island and every agent shows its whole plan, with a count of how many of its steps are done. The plan is the agent's own. The plugin gives it one tool, `island_plan`, and a rule in the global `AGENTS.md` that asks it to record the steps as it works. Delete that block and the island goes back to showing only the words. The dotted grip at the **top** moves the tab: press and drag it up or down and it slides along the edge, staying where you leave it. The grip at the **bottom** changes how long the bar is: drag it and the bar grows or shrinks downwards, its top staying put. The length you leave it at is kept, so the bar comes back the same size the next time you open OpenCode. Click anywhere else on the tab to open the island. ### The expanded island The drawer lists only the sessions that are running **now** — idle sessions stay out of the way. Each row shows: | | | |---|---| | The agent | which agent is running it | | The orb | what it is doing right now: thinking, writing, searching, running code | | The phase | `THINKING`, `WRITING`, `WORKING`, `WAITING` or `RETRYING` | | The title | what the session is about | | The tool | the tool running right now, if any | | The answer | the last words the agent said, as they stream in | | The clock | how long the session has been going | Subagents appear indented under the session that spawned them. ### Talking to an agent The drawer has a composer at its foot. It names the session the prompt will go to, and you type into the field beside it: - **Enter** sends the prompt and steers the session now. - The **menu** beside the field sends it after the current turn ends, and lists what is already waiting for that session. The chip above the field picks the session. It lists the sessions open in OpenCode, the ones you have open as tabs, the one you opened last first. A tab that is not running is still there, so a session that has ended can be talked to again. The drawer stays open while you work: it does not close when the app takes the focus back, and it does not close when you click away. It closes when you close it, by clicking the island or by pressing Escape. ### The size of the drawer The open drawer has a grip on its **bottom edge** and on its **left edge**. Drag the bottom edge and the drawer grows downwards, its top staying put. Drag the left edge and it grows leftwards, because the right edge is the screen edge and never moves. The size you leave it at is kept, so the drawer comes back the same size the next time. ### The bottom bar | Control | What it does | |---|---| | ☀️ 🌙 🖥 | Appearance, in one button: click it and it cycles light, dark, system | | ⬛ | Open OpenCode: the island floats above everything and never takes focus, so this brings the app back to the front | | ⏻ | Close everything: the island and OpenCode both go | | 👆 | Click-through: the island stops taking clicks, except its grip, so you can still open it | | 📌 ⏱ | Stay open or Auto-close: the drawer stays open when the app takes the focus back, or it closes like it used to. It stays open by default | | ☰ | Show the latest session's work in the closed tab instead of the summary | The two first buttons are also in the closed tab, at the foot of the spine above the grip that resizes it. ### Approvals When an agent asks for permission, the island turns warning orange and opens itself. Three buttons answer it in place: - **Allow once** — this one call - **Always allow** — this tool for the rest of the session - **Deny** Answering closes the island again. ## How it works The plugin has two halves, and the split is what makes it survive. **The server half** (`src/index.ts`) is an ordinary OpenCode plugin. It does nothing on its own; it exists so the desktop app discovers the package and reads its GUI bundle. **The GUI half** (`src/gui.tsx`) runs in the desktop app's **main process**. That is the important part: a window-hosted plugin would stop when the last app window closes, which is exactly when you want to know that an agent is stuck on a permission prompt. From main, the plugin also reaches the app's own server, so it sees the sessions of **every project** on your machine, not just the one you have open. ``` src/gui.tsx the plugin: follows the app's server, owns the state src/model.ts turns the server's event stream into sessions and phases src/state.ts the JSON the island renders src/window.ts the Electron window: placement, dragging, resizing src/island/app/ the island UI: React 19, Tailwind v4 and shadcn/ui src/island/preload.cjs the bridge between the page and the window ``` The island page is built by its own Vite pass into a single self-contained HTML file, which is then inlined into the plugin bundle. At runtime the island makes no network requests of its own and loads nothing from disk. The window is frameless, transparent and always on top. It is sized by the page: the page measures itself and asks the window for that size, and the window animates to it as a drawer sliding out of the screen edge on macOS, and snaps to it on Windows. The island never takes focus when it appears. ## Develop ```sh npm install # --ignore-scripts also works, and skips Electron's binary npm run dev # build the island, then watch the plugin bundle npm run typecheck # the plugin and the island, separately npm run check # the streaming tail helpers and the platform guard ``` The desktop app hot-reloads the plugin when `dist/gui-experimental.cjs` changes, so `npm run dev` is enough to see most edits. You must restart the app after changing anything that runs in the main process (`src/gui.tsx`, `src/window.ts`, `src/model.ts`). The island UI lives in `src/island/app`. It is a separate Vite build with its own TypeScript config, because the plugin's own JSX is Solid and the island's is React. ## Limits - The primary display only. - On Windows the island belongs to the virtual desktop it was opened on: Windows hides windows that belong to another desktop, and no Electron API changes that. A game in exclusive full screen covers the island too; a borderless full-screen window does not. - On Windows the island sits at the top of the always-on-top stack, so it floats over other floating windows too, and the drawer snaps open instead of sliding. - On Windows the click-through grip stops working while an elevated window has the focus: Windows does not forward mouse moves to a lower-privilege app. - The island's spot along the edge, its appearance and its switches are remembered for the session only; they reset when the app restarts. - The island shows what the app's server knows. A session that never announces itself stays invisible. ## Built by [Soussitech](https://www.soussitech.com/) — the island, the plugin and the page. ## License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
